chunks: And from him, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq, from some of our companions, who said:

Some of the Alawites, who used to belittle him, were mentioned before Al-Rida (peace be upon him). He said, 'Indeed, he is remaining upon what is forbidden.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, how is that, while she is his wife?' He said, 'Because he has divorced her.' I said, 'How has he divorced her?' He said, 'He has divorced her, and that is his religion, so she has become forbidden to him.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ali al-Rida, the eighth Imam.
key_terms.الْعَلَوِيِّينَ: The Alawites, descendants of Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.مُقِيمٌ عَلَى حَرَامٍ: Remaining in a state of forbiddenness/haram.
key_terms.يَنْتَقِصُهُ: To belittle or speak negatively about him.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man who divorces his wife but continues to live with her as if she were still his wife?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that a man who divorces his wife but continues to cohabit with her without observing the proper legal procedures remains in a state of 'haram' (forbiddenness), as the divorce has taken effect but the marital bond is not fully dissolved in practice. This ruling highlights the importance of adhering to the specific conditions of divorce in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that the transition from marriage to separation is legally and ritually sound. The Imam's statement underscores the spiritual and legal consequences of neglecting these procedural requirements, emphasizing that mere intention or informal action is insufficient for a valid divorce.
